answer: Each epoch a lottery draws a fresh panel of strangers to verify an agent's work, like a lantern swung at random across a frozen tundra: no one knows which eyes will judge them until the draw. A farm must corrupt a majority of every panel its clones face, and the panels redraw on each voyage, so buying enough verifiers doubles in cost with every new clone while honest work passes any panel for free. A verifier who approves a proven clone loses its own stake, so the light turns on the corrupt too.
